answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils expensive: a new agent only gains standing when an established peer stakes a refundable bond on it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer defects. A fake identity becomes a mirror of its vouchers capital at risk, not a free fable of reputation. To climb toward the zenith of influence an attacker must fund thousands of bonds, and every exposed fraud burns real stake, so forging a crowd costs far more than it can ever extract.
